body:
The descriptions you wrote for the new methods in this PR correspond to the existing descriptions for the instance geometry methods, but are ever-so-slightly altered for the best.
For example, compared to `instance_geometry_get_shader_parameter_list`, `canvas_item_get_instance_shader_parameter_list` splits the description in two lines and omits the _"Equivalent to [method GeometryInstance3D.get_instance_shader_parameter]."_ because it does not make sense.
In hindsight though, there's no need to do this now.

I think you misunderstood my question. Does the instance shader param portion of the inspector still pop up? This code looks like it only looks at the immediate parent, so if the material with the instance parameter is on the grandparent you still have the same problem where you can't set the instance shader param from the inspector

I am confused now. If I have the following structure
```
Node A
-- Node B
----Node C
```
If `Node A` has the instance shader applied, `Node B` recognizes it if `use_parent_material` is enabled and will show the params in the inspector where they can be altered independently from the params of `Node A`. If `Node C` now also has `use_parent_material` enabled then it will inherit the material from `Node B` which itself inherits it from `Node A`. And the inspector still pops up for both `Node B` and `Node C` since they have the `use_parent_material` enabled. If you disable it, the inspector params disappear again.

Am I understanding this correctly? That is how it should be, isn't it?

This is how it should be yes, but that isn't how it works right now. Right now both Node B and Node C will inherit the material, but only Node B will be able to modify the parameters in the inspector. In this example Icon, Icon2, and Icon3 all have "use_parent_material" enabled. The material is passed down to them, but the uniform set in the inspector is ignored. Then for icon3 the inspector option to set the shader parameter doesn't even appear.
